article_text:
T here was a time, not so long ago, when watching a film was a clearcut experience. There would be a good guy and a bad guy, and you would know who the bad guy was because they would shoot a dog in the face.

It happened more times than you might expect. Mad Max 2, dog gets shot. Revenge, dog gets shot. Turner & Hooch, dog gets shot. Red, dog gets shot. Man with the Gun, dog gets shot. Badlands, dog gets shot. Dog Soldiers, you’ll never guess.

But how things change. These days – thanks to either political correctness gone mad or basic human decency or whatever – dogs are much less likely to be murdered in films.

A study by (of course) pet insurance firm Lassie has discovered that the number of dogs that die in movies dropped by a whopping 80% between 2020 and 2025. It reports that six years ago, 10 of the 100 highest-grossing films featured a dog dying either on or off screen. But by 2025, this number fell to just two.

Now, this could be down to any number of reasons. The first, and possibly most important, is that cinema finds itself in a perilous position. The future of the entire medium is at stake and every dollar counts, so why risk alienating a swathe of the audience by gratuitously offing a pup? Things are so bad that there is an entire website – Does the Dog Die? – purely to warn viewers of any enjoyment-spoiling canine fatalities.

In fact, we may have become so sensitive to animal-related deaths onscreen that it has been offered as one potential reason for the Digger flop. After all, the film’s trailer heavily focused on Digger’s sick cat as it was given a terminal diagnosis. Now obviously it was a deliberately bad animatronic prop cat, but that didn’t stop large numbers of Does the Dog Die?’s users from warning people of its death.

So nervous are we as an audience that film-makers cannot even make dog movies without explicitly reassuring us that the animals are going to make it out OK. As early as June, Richard Raymond – the producer of Brad Pitt’s new canine movie Heart of the Beast – took to social media to literally spoil the ending of his own film, just to set our minds at rest, tweeting: “The dog does not die. You’re welcome.”

And then there’s Anne Hathaway, whose film The End of Oak Street concerns a family, a dog, and a very hungry T rex. During promotion for the (12A) film, Hathaway tacitly managed to reassure audiences that the dog wasn’t going to become dino chow, by stating that “I feel like movies that kill dogs should automatically be rated R.”

Of course, however, this leads me to suspect that Anne Hathaway hasn’t actually watched all of her films. Her highest-grossing of the year was Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey , which features a dog death so absolutely gratuitous that it legitimately borders on slapstick. In short, a dog gets hurled off a cliff. Is it central to the story? No, it isn’t even remotely peripheral to the story. It’s just a thing that happens. The sun rises. The sun sets. John Leguizamo lobs a puppy off the side of a cliff.

Obviously Hathaway is wrong here. An automatic R-rating for a dog death would change the texture of films as we know them. In Turner & Hooch, Hooch’s death was the entire point of the movie. Did it permanently traumatise a generation of children who thought they had signed up for a funny dog flick? Yes. But did it also work to brace us better against the cruel realities of the world? Also yes.

And perhaps that’s what we all need. We live in deeply uncertain times, and sometimes it feels like we still aren’t fully prepared for the horrors that await us. So ask yourself this: is this the right time to cosset ourselves away from things that upset us, or is it time that film-makers started to act responsibly again by killing as many dogs as they possibly can? It doesn’t matter what sort of film it is, whether it’s a drama or a horror or a Paw Patrol cartoon. Let’s impose a mandatory canine death quota to toughen us up again.

Who’s with me? Nobody? What if it was just Paw Patrol, then? What if it was just Chase from Paw Patrol? Still no? Suit yourselves.

article_text:
Boo Junfeng ’s “ Trinity ” and Sidharta Tata’s “Slaughterground” are among 11 feature projects picked for JAFF Future Project (JFP), the film development strand of Indonesia’s JAFF Market , which has also chosen 10 intellectual properties for its adaptation-focused JAFF IP Connection (JIPCon) program.

The third edition of JAFF Market, powered by Amar Bank, will run Nov. 28–30 at the Jogja Expo Center in Yogyakarta, during the Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival (Nov. 28–Dec. 5). One of the film projects comes from Australia through a partnership with the Adelaide Film Festival and mylab, while two Korean IPs join via a tie-up with the Asian Contents & Film Market (ACFM).

Related Stories

AI Could ‘Absolutely’ Replace Human Actors, CEO of Generative AI Startup Runway Says at Italy's View Conference: 'It's Already Happening in a Way'

AI Giant Nvidia Invests in Entertainment Startup Higgsfield

“Trinity” (original title “Tsai Kuang Chih Chien”) is one of two works in progress in the selection and lists the widest spread of production countries: Taiwan, France, Singapore, Poland, Greece, Germany, Japan, Brazil, South Korea, Indonesia and the Philippines. Peanut Pictures is the production company, with Raymond Phathanavirangoon, Sophie Erbs, Aileen Li, Huang Junxiang and Boo producing.

Popular on Variety

The other work in progress is Tata’s “Slaughterground” (“Hujan Kematian”), produced by Ajish Dibyo, Pramudya Andika, Annisa Adjam and Sunny Gho for Aftersun Creative. The remaining nine projects are in development.

Among them is M. Raihan Halim’s Singapore project “The Smuggler,” produced by Asra Aman for Papahan Films. Two Indonesian women directors are at work on what will be their first features: Ninndi Raras with “A Quiet Sunshine” (“Perempuan di Pulau Lea”), produced by Giovanni Rahmadeva and Siera Tamihardja for QUN Films, and Dian Tamara with “Somewhere Between” (“Titik Temu”), from Gambar Gerak and Pancaran Sinema with Arya Ibrahim and Moch. As’ad Azwin producing.

Also from Indonesia are Dhiwangkara Seta’s “αLPα (Absence),” from Lune Features; Timoteus Anggawan Kusno’s “Orphaned Atlas” (“Sampar”), an Indonesia, France and Netherlands project from Forka Films produced by Ifa Isfansyah and Agustiya Herdwiyanto; and Rein Maychaelson’s “Primal,” a Studio Rumah Kedua project listing Indonesia, Singapore and South Korea as production countries. Yudhatama Fajar Nugroho’s “Pupus: The Orchid of Merapi” (“Pupus: Anggrek Merapi”) from Manimonki Studio is the only animated title. Glenn Barit’s “Luz and Flor” (“Luzonensis and Floresiensis”), produced by Kristine De Leon and Tanveer Hossain for Katalog, represents the Philippines.

Taken together, the films deal with family, faith, memory, identity and migration, in forms that range from close-quarters drama to genre work.

The Australian entry is Rosie Lourde’s “Wreck and Ruin,” which Lourde is producing with Katharine McPhee for In Cahoots Creations.

“Our partnership with JAFF Market and mylab gives Australian filmmakers an opportunity to engage with the region’s creative and production networks while their projects are still taking shape,” said Mat Kesting, CEO and creative director of the Adelaide Film Festival. “We want these exchanges to build a stronger foundation for collaboration, connecting teams with partners who can contribute to development, financing and the international journey of their films.”

Lorna Tee, founder of mylab, said international collaboration starts with understanding a filmmaker’s vision and what each partner can bring. “Through our collaboration with JAFF Market and Adelaide Film Festival, we want to connect Australian filmmaking teams with producers in Indonesia and across Asia, building relationships that can shape their films and continue beyond the market,” she said.

On the IP side, six of the 10 selections are Indonesian. They are “Komarong,” represented by Gilang Bhagaskara; the board game “Mantra,” represented by Sigit Ezra Prayoga; the comics “Darah di Atas Salju” (“Blood Upon the Snow”), represented by Dedy, “Lao Sam 1892,” represented by Toni Masdiono, and “Yuuko’s Gloomy Days,” represented by Anwita Citriya; and the novel “Hati-Hati Ada Dua Hati,” represented by Ario Tamat.

The selection also takes in two IPs from Hong Kong and Taiwan: the comic “Disposable Dolly,” represented by Ben Liu, and the book “Cat Rental Company,” represented by Maka (Zhou Lishu). The ACFM pair are the book “My Upstairs Neighbors,” represented by Clayhouse Inc., and webtoon “Friend Request,” represented by Ryoung Studio.

Both slates will also feed into JAFF Market’s first Producers Exchange, which will set up meetings between participating producers and the JFP teams, JIPCon representatives, exhibitors and other delegates.

“We want producers to come to JAFF Market knowing they can discover films taking shape and original IP with potential for the screen,” said Linda Gozali, market director of JAFF Market. “JFP and JIPCon bring filmmakers and IP representatives into conversation with partners who can contribute creatively, help structure financing and connect stories with audiences. Our ambition is to turn that discovery into lasting collaboration and strengthen Indonesia’s role as a creative and production partner.”

The Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival was founded in 2006.

article_text:
EXCLUSIVE: Global nonfiction entertainment studio XTR is coming on board Y Vân: The Lost Sounds of Saigon as the award-winning documentary ramps up its campaign for Oscar recognition.

That bid was strengthened over the weekend as the film directed by Khoa Hà and Victor Velle won the Audience Award at the New Orleans Film Festival.

The documentary follows Khoa “as she sets out to recover the lost musical recordings of her late grandfather, legendary Vietnamese composer Y Vân, who the film colloquially refers to as ‘The Quincy Jones of Saigon,’” notes a release. “Y Vân was one of the most prolific and famous composers in Vietnam during the 50s, 60s, and 70s, but by the end of the war, most of his original recordings had been lost or destroyed.”

Related Stories

acTVe Acquires Documentary+ Streaming Platform; CEO Geoff Clark Vows To Turn It Into "The Netflix Of Documentaries"

AI Firm Moonvalley Releases "Commercially Safe" Marey Video System To General Public

“Blending vérité filmmaking, archival discoveries, and poetic animation, the film traces a deeply personal search across generations, continents, and the history of Vietnam,” according to a synopsis. “It has received rave reviews from Vietnamese communities around the country, and has been met with large crowds and sold out shows throughout the summer. Notably, audiences have been composed of multiple generations – kids, teens, parents, and grandparents – bringing all ages together in a collective experience.”

Watch on Deadline

XTR founders Bryn Mooser and Justin Lacob join Y Vân as executive producers. Mooser, a two-time Academy Award nominee ( Lifeboat , Body Team 12 ), calls the film “entertaining, visually stunning, and full of adventure. A profoundly important film for Vietnamese-Americans and the world at large, reminding us that love, family, and music can heal the wounds of war.”

Y Vân: The Lost Sounds of Saigon premiered in competition at DOC NYC in 2025. In addition to the Audience Award at the New Orleans Film Festival, it won the Grand Jury Award for Best Documentary Feature at the Atlanta Film Festival, Best Feature Film at Viet Film Festival, and the Audience Award for Best Documentary Feature and the Audience Award for Best of Festival at the San Luis Obispo International Film Festival, among other honors. It has also been named to the Top 10 Most Popular Films at DOCNYC.

The documentary is set for a theatrical release in early 2027. In conjunction with that, the film team will be releasing the newly recovered, restored and remastered original recordings of Y Vân through exclusive vinyl pressings.

Y Vân: The Lost Sounds of Saigon is a production of The Pink Cloud, directed by Khoa Hà and Victor Velle, and produced by Douglas Emerson.

Der Profihändler GraphicArt führt zwei Sony-Fotowalks für Freunde der Vogelfotografie durch, bei denen u. a. die diversen Supertele-Neuheiten der vergangenen Monate ausprobiert werden können. Bei so einem kostenlosen Fotowalk werden Teilnehmer von einem erfahrenen Fotoprofi durch das Gelände eines BirdLife-Naturzentrums mit seinen vielen Vogelarten geführt. Dabei haben die Teilnehmer die Möglichkeit, Kameras und Objektive in der Praxis auszuprobieren. Überdies erhalten sie auch Tipps und Anregungen zur Vogelfotografie vom jeweiligen Profifotografen.

Der eine Fotowalk findet am Donnerstag, 1 2. November 2026, in La Sauge beim Neuenburgersee mit dem Naturfotografen Adrian Schmid statt – Infos dazu finden Sie im separaten Artikel . Der andere Fotowalk wird am Freitag, 13. November 2026, in Neerach mit dem Fotoprofi Lukas Moesch durchgeführt. Zusätzlich gibt es noch eine Lightroom-Demonstration über die Bearbeitung von Vogelbildern. Zur Veranstaltung in Neerach finden Sie nachfolgend weitere Infos.

Begleiten Sie den Naturfotograf Lukas Moesch auf einem spannenden, kostenlosen Fotowalk durch das BirdLife-Naturzentrum Neeracherried, das sich nördlich von Dielsdorf und des Flughafens Kloten-Zürich befindet. Für diesen Anlass ist das Naturzentrum exklusiv für die Teilnehmenden geöﬀnet .

Entdecken Sie die faszinierende Tierwelt, lernen Sie spannende Perspektiven kennen und erhalten Sie wertvolle Tipps für eindrucksvolle Wildlife-Aufnahmen. Nutzen Sie die Gelegenheit, gemeinsam mit Lukas Moesch zu fotografieren und Ihr Wissen direkt in der Praxis zu vertiefen.

Im Anschluss an den Fotowalk zeigt Dave Brunner, der Gewinner des BirdLife-Fotowettbewerb 2026, in einer Lightroom-Demonstration, wie er seine Bilder bearbeitet. Er gibt Einblicke in seinen Workflow und vermittelt praktische Tipps für die Bearbeitung eigener Wildlife-Aufnahmen.

Kameras und Objektive kostenlos ausprobieren: Vor Ort steht eine grosse Auswahl an Sony-Kameras und Objektiven zum Testen bereit.

Beratung : Fachleute von Sony und GraphicArt geben Auskunft über die Sony-Produkte und beantworten Fragen der Teilnehmer.

Anmeldung: Die Teilnahme ist kostenlos. Fünf Zeitfenster stehen am 13.11.2026 zur Wahl.

editorial_title_zh: 森林与城市在达维德·帕卢萨于的里雅斯特街头的摄影作品中相互交叠

article_text:
Un bosco e una città sembrano appartenere a ordini diversi ma entrambi sono spazi di convivenza. Nel primo, specie differenti, animali e vegetali, animate e inanimate, condividono risorse, habitat e cicli di nascita, crescita e morte seguendo i ritmi delle stagioni. Nella seconda, corpi, infrastrutture, merci e attività si organizzano secondo logiche antropiche, senza però riuscire a sottrarsi completamente agli eventi naturali. Alluvioni, terremoti, raffiche di vento, ondate di calore, anche lo spazio urbano continua a essere esposto a forze che ne mettono in crisi la presunta autonomia, con una frequenza e un impatto accentuati dagli effetti del cambiamento climatico.

È in questa sovrapposizione che si inserisce Bosco manifesto , mostra a cielo aperto di Davide Maria Palusa , curata da Lorenzo Lazzari e prodotta da Adriatico Book Club , visibile a Trieste fino al 31 ottobre 2026. Venti manifesti di grande formato portano nelle strade della città fotografie realizzate nel Bosco Bovedo, creando un confronto diretto tra ecosistema naturale e paesaggio urbanizzato.

Il bosco dentro la città: il dispositivo di Davide Palusa

Segni impressi sulla corteccia, strutture avvolte dalla vegetazione, stagni artificiali trasformati in habitat per specie selvatiche, alberi affacciati verso il porto. Le immagini di Palusa non cercano un’idea incontaminata di natura ma mostrano un paesaggio di confine, dove l’azione umana e i processi naturali si sovrappongono continuamente.

Collocate in contesti fortemente urbanizzati, le fotografie introducono una dissonanza visiva. Da lontano funzionano come aperture improvvise sul Bovedo. Avvicinandosi, il testo che accompagna ciascun manifesto restituisce il contesto della ricerca e pone alcune domande: «E se il bosco non ci fosse più? Quali conseguenze avrebbe la sua scomparsa sulla mitigazione del cambiamento climatico in città? Quale perdita comporterebbe per il paesaggio?».

Il dispositivo espositivo trasferisce così il bosco fuori dai propri confini e lo porta nello spazio quotidiano della città, suggerendo che i due ambienti non siano separati quanto appaiono.

Un ecosistema tra mare, città e montagna

Il Bosco Bovedo costituisce un’area naturale di particolare interesse per la sua posizione e per la compresenza di specie provenienti da habitat mediterranei, alpini e balcanici. Situato tra il mare, la città e l’altipiano carsico, il bosco partecipa anche alla regolazione del microclima urbano, alla qualità dell’aria e alla mitigazione del dissesto idrogeologico. La sua funzione non è quindi soltanto paesaggistica ma riguarda direttamente gli equilibri ambientali di Trieste.

Su questo territorio agiscono però pressioni differenti. Da una parte gli effetti del cambiamento climatico. Dall’altra la prospettiva di nuove infrastrutture, tra cui la Cabinovia Metropolitana Trieste-Opicina, progetto la cui idea risale al 2020 e che prevede due tratte e quattro stazioni su un tragitto di circa 4,7 chilometri, dal centro di Trieste all’Altopiano del Carso. Se il progetto è stato da subito accompagnato da numerose proteste da parte della cittadinanza e di associazioni territoriali, Bosco manifesto si inserisce in questa condizione senza voler restituire una rappresentazione didascalica del conflitto, concentrandosi piuttosto sulle relazioni minute che tengono insieme il luogo.

Le tracce dell’abitare

Come osserva il curatore Lorenzo Lazzari, «Lo sguardo di Palusa cerca di restituire nella fotografia non una rappresentazione idilliaca del bosco, ma un ecosistema complesso, che è fatto anche da interazioni antropiche quotidiane con l’ambiente naturale».

Queste interazioni emergono attraverso oggetti, segni e piccole architetture, elementi che rivelano come il bosco sia già attraversato da pratiche umane. La fotografia assume allora un carattere quasi ricognitivo, attento a ciò che normalmente resta ai margini dello sguardo. Lazzari sottolinea infatti come molte di queste tracce siano diventate visibili grazie al rapporto costruito da Palusa con gli abitanti, capaci di introdurre l’artista dentro una conoscenza del luogo che non si esaurisce nella semplice osservazione.

Una ricerca partecipata

Il progetto nasce da un’indagine condotta sul campo che combina fotografia, interviste e confronto con competenze provenienti dall’ornitologia, dalla botanica e dalla geologia. Questo intreccio di saperi permette di leggere il Bosco Bovedo come un sistema di relazioni. La fotografia diventa così uno strumento attraverso cui far emergere connessioni tra ambiente naturale e costruito, memoria locale e trasformazioni in corso.

Formato in architettura, Davide Maria Palusa sviluppa da tempo una ricerca sul rapporto tra spazio, paesaggio e osservazione. Nei suoi lavori architetture e ambienti naturali funzionano contemporaneamente come soggetti e come scenari, facendo emergere ciò che esiste dentro e fuori l’immagine.

Bosco manifesto si concluderà con la pubblicazione di un libro fotografico che raccoglierà una selezione più ampia delle immagini realizzate da Palusa. Un ulteriore passaggio di un progetto che, dalla ricerca sul campo alla strada e infine alla pagina, interroga il rapporto tra ambiente naturale e spazio antropizzato.

Tutt’intorno alla fiera Art Basel Paris, dal 19 al 25 ottobre 2026 la città si trasforma in un paesaggio espositivo diffuso, che si snoda tra raffinate dimore storiche, padiglioni temporanei e spazi di ricerca indipendente. Dal design d’autore alla fotografia, dalle vivaci scene africane e asiatiche ai progetti curatoriali delle gallerie emergenti, le “altre” fiere parigine contribuiscono ad ampliare il dialogo dell’arte del Novecento con le sperimentazioni contemporanee e le nuove generazioni di artisti. In questo palcoscenico unico, la dimensione commerciale si intreccia nuovamente con la scoperta culturale e il dibattito critico, restituendo un quadro vivo e in continua evoluzione del mercato dell’arte contemporaneo.

Design Miami Paris

Dal 21 al 25 ottobre 2026, Design Miami Paris torna all’Hôtel de Maisons (51 rue de l’Université). La quarta edizione trasforma la dimora settecentesca del Faubourg Saint-Germain in un luogo d’incontro tra design storico, creazione contemporanea e artigianato. Accanto alle gallerie e alle installazioni del programma Design at Large, torna la collaborazione con Apple per Designers of Tomorrow: quattro talenti emergenti esplorano la capacità del design di creare connessioni. Il programma si estende al 72 rue de l’Université con il progetto di Jordan Roth, tra scultura, arredo e memoria personale. La fiera apre dalle 11 alle 19, con chiusura alle 18 nell’ultima giornata.

Paris Internationale

Dal 20 al 24 ottobre 2026, Paris Internationale presenta la sua dodicesima edizione in una nuova sede al 187–189 quai de Valmy, nel quartiere del Canal Saint-Martin. La manifestazione riunisce 56 gallerie e cinque spazi non profit provenienti da 19 Paesi, con quindici gallerie al debutto. Questa edizione sceglie una scala più concentrata, per lasciare maggiore spazio ai progetti e favorire una visita attenta, senza separare gallerie emergenti e affermate in settori distinti. L’edificio di 3.500 metri quadrati, articolato in due corpi e quattro cortili, accoglie un allestimento sviluppato da Christ & Gantenbein e interventi site-specific. L’ingresso è gratuito ed è aperto al pubblico dal 20 al 24 ottobre: martedì dalle 11 alle 19, da mercoledì a venerdì dalle 12 alle 19 e sabato dalle 12 alle 18.

AKAA – Also Known As Africa

Dal 23 al 25 ottobre 2026, AKAA torna al Carreau du Temple (4, rue Eugène Spuller) per la sua undicesima edizione. La fiera dedicata alla creazione africana e afrodiscendente assegna quest’anno un ruolo centrale alla fotografia, richiamandone il bicentenario. Fulcro dell’edizione è “Mother’s Heritage” di Gabriel Dia: fotografie di grande formato stampate su tessuto e sospese come abiti stesi, in un racconto intimo di eredità familiare e identità di genere. Il percorso “La mémoire des feuilles” valorizza invece disegni, collage e altre opere su carta. L’apertura al pubblico è dalle 12 alle 20 il 23 e 24 ottobre e dalle 12 alle 18 il 25 ottobre.

ASIA NOW

Dal 20 al 24 ottobre 2026, ASIA NOW torna alla Monnaie de Paris (11 quai de Conti). La dodicesima edizione si sviluppa attorno al tema “Sentimental Value”, interrogando il valore che le opere acquistano attraverso ricordi, relazioni ed esperienze personali. L’arte asiatica e delle sue diaspore emerge così come un territorio in movimento, attraversato da migrazioni, scambi e trasformazioni culturali, anziché come una realtà circoscritta da confini geografici. La fiera, aperta tutti i giorni dalle 11 alle 19, conferma il suo intento di superare la contrapposizione tra Oriente e Occidente, dando spazio a voci meno visibili e privilegiando, accanto alla dimensione commerciale, le relazioni e il confronto culturale.

OFFSCREEN

Dal 20 al 25 ottobre 2026, OFFSCREEN torna alla Chapelle Saint-Louis de la Salpêtrière (47 boulevard de l’Hôpital, nel tredicesimo arrondissement). La quinta edizione riunisce 29 artisti attorno alle possibilità espressive dell’immagine fissa e in movimento, attraverso un percorso di installazioni in dialogo con l’architettura della cappella. Ospite d’onore è Ana Mendieta, alla quale è dedicata una presentazione di sei film nella rotonda centrale, tra corpo, natura e ritualità. Fotografia, cinema e sperimentazione digitale attraversano così generazioni e linguaggi diversi. Completa il programma “Acquisitions and Discoveries”, con opere provenienti dalla Pinault Collection e dal Whitney Museum of American Art, rafforzando il confronto tra ricerca artistica, istituzioni e collezionismo. La fiera è aperta al pubblico dal 20 al 24 ottobre dalle 11 alle 19 e domenica 25 ottobre dalle 11 alle 18.

Moderne Art Fair

Moderne Art Fair torna dal 22 al 25 ottobre 2026 nei padiglioni temporanei della splendida Place de la Concorde. L’edizione riunisce 55 gallerie costruendo un dialogo tra Novecento e ricerca contemporanea. Ospite d’onore è l’Institut du monde arabe , che riunisce sette artisti, tra cui Etel Adnan, Shafic Abboud, Baya e Dia Al-Azzawi, restituendo la pluralità della modernità artistica dei mondi arabi. La fiera è aperta dalle 11 alle 20, con chiusura alle 18 domenica 25 ottobre.

Post-Fair Paris

Dal 19 al 24 ottobre 2026, Post-Fair approda a Parigi con la sua prima edizione europea, ospitata in due spazi storici al 74 e al 79 rue du Temple, nel Marais. Fondata dal gallerista Chris Sharp e inaugurata l’anno scorso a Los Angeles, la manifestazione nasce come alternativa alle fiere tradizionali per favorire un incontro più diretto con le opere. L’esordio parigino riunisce 34 espositori internazionali e il percorso si propone come una mostra curata, nella quale l’architettura delle due sedi contribuisce all’esperienza di visita. L’ingresso è gratuito: il 19 ottobre il pubblico è accolto dalle 17 alle 20, dopo l’anteprima riservata; dal 20 al 24 ottobre l’apertura è dalle 11 alle 18.

editorial_excerpt_zh: 蕾雅·赛杜饰演的妻子兼母亲在警察上门盘问丈夫后生活分崩离析；耶拉·哈斯饰演的侦探正在处理她生病父亲的不端行为。玛丽·克鲁策是奥地利导演，曾创作过心理惊悚片《地心之基》和哈布斯堡王朝传记片《束缚》等令人印象深刻且风格独特的作品……

article_text:
M arie Kreutzer is the Austrian director who created impressive and stylish pictures such as the psychological thriller The Ground Beneath My Feet and the Habsburg biopic Corsage . Now she brings us this coldly eloquent and disquieting Franco-German drama about two women who find themselves imprisoned by a duty of care and loyalty to the men in their lives. One discovers something terrible about her husband and immediately goes into a state of negotiated denial, the other loves her demanding job as a police officer, and is all the more dependent on the live-in cleaner/care worker who looks after her difficult elderly father.

Léa Seydoux plays the first, Lucy Weiss, a French musician who has built up an enthusiastic, though niche following for her experimental pop-classical hybrid performances. Her mother, played in cameo by Catherine Deneuve , was a more conventionally successful concert pianist. Lucy has a comfortable home in Munich with her German TV director husband, Philip (Laurence Rupp), and their lively nine-year-old son, Johnny (Malo Blanchet). But Philip has had a breakdown, collapsing sobbing in Lucy’s arms, apparently due to overwork and drug problems. She agrees to move to the countryside to soothe his emotional pain, and for a while things look better. Philip is evidently devoted to Johnny, playfully filming him and Lucy for some little personal project, and manfully building his son a trampoline in the garden.

But then Elsa, played by Jella Haase, a detective with the Munich police, shows up at their front door, accompanied by an intimidating array of about half a dozen uniformed officers with a search warrant, demanding to take away all Philip’s computers, tablets and smartphones. Stunned, Lucy asks Elsa – and Philip – what this is all about, and Philip, though clearly in no doubt, is unable to answer.

Haase’s performance gives Elsa a fierce, calm, professional cop’s gaze: uncompromising but not confrontational with her hair tied back; this is very different from Lucy’s tousled, often sleepy sensuality, which from this moment disintegrates into a kind of horror, like a sleepwalker shaken awake. As for Philip’s expression, Kreutzer cleverly invites us to compare it to another case that Elsa and her criminal division are investigating. They show up at a suspect’s door and the man of the house opens it, sees the police, realises in the next moment what this is about, but his instant denial and aversion keeps his expression politely blank as he asks if he can help.

As for Philip, he spins Lucy a number of fatuous lies: that he was looking at this material on chat groups and online picture-sharing forums as research for a new documentary – or, even more implausibly, that he was just brokering these images for “the money”, to afford this new country home. And Lucy’s own ordeal is her need to believe him, to twist and contort what she sees so it will fit into Philip’s shapeshifting explanations. As for Elsa, she is unbending in her pursuit of the wrongdoer at work, but at home desperately makes excuses for her father, Hermann (Sylvester Groth), when he inappropriately harasses his care worker, Natalia (Patrycja Ziółkowska).

The central point is whether all this involves Johnny; Philip swears it does not but Elsa says that, despite the police child psychiatrist and doctor finding no evidence of abuse, one can never be sure, and it is this not knowing which is the drama’s agony. This is a bleak, pessimistic film with two excellent lead performances.

article_text:
自画像 47KMのおとぎ話

劇場公開日： 2026年11月16日

解説・あらすじ

中国のドキュメンタリー監督ジャン・モンチーが、父の故郷である湖北省の村を10年以上にわたって記録してきた「自画像 47KM」シリーズ第9作。子どもたちが描いた絵から村に新たな公共空間が生まれていく過程を見つめる。 村は「47KM」と呼ばれ、山あいの集落には老人と子どもたちが暮らしている。10度目の冬、幼い女の子が「大きな青い家を作るよ」と声を上げる。それは村人が集い、子どもたちが学ぶ場として監督が長年思い描いてきた空間だった。子どもたちはどんな家にしたいかを想像し、次々と絵に描いていく。描かれたおとぎ話は、やがて丘の上で現実の建物として形を取り始める。カメラを手にした子どもたちは家族を撮り始め、建ちかけの家でパフォーマンスを繰り広げていく。 監督のジャン・モンチーはダンサー・振付家として活動しながら2010年に47KM村での撮影を始め、2020年には村に家を建てて移住し 、本作は第26回釜山国際映画祭のドキュメンタリー部門でメセナ賞、プント・デ・ヴィスタ映画祭2022で最優秀監督賞と青年審査員賞を受賞し、山形国際ドキュメンタリー映画祭2021インターナショナルコンペティションでも披露。シリーズ全10作をそろえた特集上映（2026年11月7～20日＝ポレポレ東中野）で上映。

2021年製作／109分／中国 原題または英題：Self-Portrait: Window in 47KM 劇場公開日：2026年11月16日

title_original: 不朽の名作・佐内正史の初写真集『生きている』が待望の復刊！復刊記念展&トークも
editorial_title_zh: 不朽名作、佐内正史首部摄影集《生きている》众望所归复刊！复刊纪念展&对谈活动也将举行
editorial_excerpt_zh: 佐内正史的首部摄影集《生きている》得以复刊。本书于1997年4月出版，当时，这批既非决定性瞬间、也非私摄影、此前无人见过的照片群引起巨大反响，让世人认识到一位新的才华。

article_text:
佐内正史の初めての写真集『生きている』が復刊を遂げる。本書は1997年4月に刊行されたが、当時、決定的瞬間ではない、私写真でもない、誰も見たことがなかった写真群は大きな反響を呼び、新たな才能を世の中が知るところとなった。その衝撃は次世代の写真家にも影響を与え、新しい写真の潮流を生み、写真史的にもエポックな出来事として記憶されている。その後『生きている』は版を重ねたものの、写真集の本文に使っていた用紙が生産中止となったことで、2007年の重版を最後に今では手に入れられなくなった写真集となっていた。

そんな中、2025年10月に創立30周年を迎えた青幻舎のメモリアルイヤースペシャル企画として、もう手に入らなくなった本の復刊プロジェクトが立ち上がる。読者からのリクエストによって、この『生きている』が晴れて復刊を遂げることとなった。

復刊には、初版『生きている』のブックデザインを手がけた造本家の町口覚氏監修の元、新たな本文用紙選定のための印刷テストを重ね、ようやくオリジナルの代わりとなる用紙に辿り着いたことで進んでいった。印刷は当時の方法に拘り、製版フィルムを使用して版を焼き、油性インクで印刷されている。一方、装丁は表紙のイメージをアップデートし、復刊として生まれ変わった新たな仕上がりとなった。刊行から29年、写真の歴史に新たなページが加わる。

さらに復刊記念として、福岡を皮切りに京都、名古屋、盛岡、広島を巡る 刊行記念展や会期中トークイベント の開催も。東京では10月11日、青山ブックセンター本店での佐内と町口によるトークイベントが予定されている。この機会をお見逃しなく。

article_text:
Cine

¿Austin Butler consideraría aparecer en la película de Zoey 101?

Antonio G. Spíndola

El nominado al Óscar habla de la posibilidad de tener un cameo en la secuela de la serie producida por Nickelodeon.

Con una destacada participación en la actual temporada de premios, el actor protagónico de Elvis (2022) probablemente ostente un luminoso porvenir dentro de Hollywood. Por lo pronto, es un hecho que tendrá un papel clave en la venidera cinta Dune: Parte 2 , del prominente director Denis Villeneuve. Pero, ¿acaso Austin Butler estaría dispuesto a voltear hacia el pasado, hacia los inicios de su carrera, y en virtud de esa nostalgia, aparecer en la venidera película de Zoey 101 ?

Recordemos que, antes de dar el salto a la pantalla grande, el histrión californiano figuró en populares shows juveniles, empezando por Hannah Montana de Disney, y las series de Nickelodeon iCarly y Zoey 101 . En esta última, Austin Butler encarnó a James Garrett, un personaje recurrente de la temporada 4, nuevo estudiante de la Academia Costa del Pacífico (PCA), imán de chicas y que durante un tiempo fue novio de la protagonista, Zoey Brooks.

Ahora bien, apenas en enero de 2023, Nickelodeon y la actriz estelar Jamie Lynn Spears anunciaron que una película secuela de Zoey 101 —titulada provisionalmente “ Zoey 102 ”— había iniciado filmaciones. Desde entonces se reportó que gran parte del elenco original estaría de vuelta.

Por otro lado, en reciente entrevista con Variety , Butler fue cuestionado directamente si estaría abierto a regresar. Sin embargo, el histrión reveló no estar al tanto de tal proyecto y se mostró dudoso respecto a la simple idea de tener un cameo.

“No he oído nada al respecto”, expresó el actor. “Pero no lo sé. Estoy muy agradecido por todos esos peldaños que he tenido a lo largo de mi carrera. Zoey 101 fue un gran punto de inflexión para mí porque era la primera vez que era un actor regular en un programa. Así que llegué a ser parte de una temporada entera”.

También te podría interesar: Austin Butler recuerda sus primeros papeles en Nickelodeon y Disney

Además de agradecer profundamente el impulso que le dieron Zoey 101 y todas aquellas series que marcaron el inicio de su trayectoria, Austin Butler recalcó que ahora su prioridad es perseguir historias que en él “resuenen” o proyectos con directores e intérpretes “con los que realmente quiera trabajar”.

“Recuerdo cuando tuve mi primera línea en un programa televisivo y eso fue algo enorme para mí. Hay todos estos momentos diferentes que resultan fundamentales para uno”, compartió con Variety . “Pero ahora sólo voy detrás de cualquier historia que resuene conmigo o cualquier director o actores con los que realmente quiera trabajar”.

La película de Zoey 101 estará ambientada varios años después de los eventos finales de la serie primigenia. Ilustrará un reencuentro de las y los exalumnos de la PCA, con motivo de una boda. Dirige Nancy Hower y su lanzamiento está previsto para este 2023 a través de Paramount Plus.

Austin Butler viene de obtener el BAFTA 2023 por Mejor actor principal gracias a su alabado trabajo en la cinta biográfica Elvis . Este papel le valió también el Globo de Oro y asimismo propició nominaciones en los Critics Choice Awards, los Premios del Sindicato de Actores y la 95° entrega de los Premios de la Academia.

Antonio G. Spíndola Tengo muy mala memoria. Por solidaridad con mis recuerdos, opto por perderme también. De preferencia, en una sala de cine.
